name: OWSM v4 Training Dataset
description: A curated multilingual speech dataset comprising 320,000 hours of audio across 151 languages, created by combining cleaned YODAS data (166,000 hours across 75 languages) with previous OWSM v3.2 data (154,000 hours). The dataset is designed for training open Whisper-style speech foundation models supporting automatic speech recognition (ASR), speech translation (ST), language identification (LID), and voice activity detection (VAD).

creator.name: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe
creator.affiliation: Carnegie Mellon University, Honda Research Institute Japan

inLanguage: mul (75 languages in cleaned YODAS, 151 languages total)
citeAs: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe. OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning. Interspeech 2025.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset combines two sources: (1) YODAS - a large-scale web-crawled dataset with Creative Commons license containing 370k hours of audio in 149 languages, providing unsegmented long-form audio recordings from diverse speaking styles and acoustic environments, and (2) previous OWSM v3.2 data. YODAS is distinctive in that it publicly releases audio files rather than links to original sources, simplifying data downloading and providing static sources for redistribution.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: (1) YODAS web-crawled dataset with 370k hours of audio in 149 languages, and (2) OWSM v3.2 dataset. YODAS provides unsegmented long-form recordings with text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-step data-cleaning pipeline was applied to YODAS: (1) Resegmentation: Realigned audio and text using CTC segmentation algorithm with OWSM-CTC v3.2 model, segmenting long-form recordings into utterances with maximum 30-second duration and removing non-speech elements like music. This reduced data from 370k to 345k hours across 83 languages. (2) LID-based filtering: Performed language identification on both audio (using ECAPA-TDNN from SpeechBrain) and text (using fastText), retaining only utterances where original language label matched both predictions. This yielded 284k hours across 75 languages. (3) CTC-score-based filtering: Removed utterances with low-quality audio-text alignments using CTC confidence scores, applying a threshold of θCTC = 0.10 (10th quantile). Final dataset contains 166k hours across 75 languages. Speech features use 128 Mel filterbanks with 8x subsampling, resulting in 80ms time shift.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: YODAS provides text transcriptions with start and end timestamps. However, these timestamps were found to be inaccurate and required realignment using CTC segmentation. Each utterance after CTC segmentation was assigned a confidence score quantifying alignment quality between audio and text.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: CTC confidence scores were used to assess annotation quality. Language-dependent ranking of scores within each language was performed. For each long-form utterance, if any constituent short utterances fell within the lowest θCTC quantile (10%), the entire utterance was discarded. Quality assessment through fine-tuning experiments showed that without filtering (θCTC = 0.00), models exhibited poor and unstable performance with WERs exceeding 100% due to token repetitions, confirming substantial misalignment issues in raw data.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: OWSM-CTC v3.2 model for CTC segmentation and confidence scoring, ECAPA-TDNN from SpeechBrain for spoken language identification, fastText for text-based language identification
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The cleaned YODAS data, pre-trained models, training code, and training logs will be publicly released via the ESPnet toolkit. YODAS establishes a scalable pipeline to crawl data from the web, and future versions can further grow beyond the current 370k hours.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset covers 75 languages in the cleaned YODAS portion and 151 languages total, representing diverse linguistic and geographic attributes. The top 10 languages by duration in cleaned YODAS are: English (74.6k hours), Spanish (17.3k hours), Russian (15.7k hours), Portuguese (10.8k hours), Korean (10.9k hours), French (8.6k hours), German (7.1k hours), Italian (5.6k hours), Vietnamese (4.6k hours), and Indonesian (3.3k hours). The distribution across languages is highly imbalanced, with English constituting the largest share while many other languages remain underrepresented.
rai:dataBiases: The distribution across languages is highly imbalanced. English constitutes the largest share (74.6k hours out of 166k total in cleaned YODAS), whereas many other languages continue to be underrepresented. The original distribution was kept without any resampling. The raw YODAS data contained incorrect language labels and audio-text misalignments, which were addressed through the cleaning pipeline.
rai:dataLimitations: Common issues in the raw YODAS data include mismatched language labels and misalignment between audio and text. The OWSM-CTC v3.2 model used for CTC segmentation supports only a subset of the languages present in YODAS (83 out of 149 languages). The language distribution is highly imbalanced, with English dominating and many languages underrepresented. The data cleaning process required careful threshold selection, as performance trends varied across different test sets.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training speech foundation models supporting multiple tasks: automatic speech recognition (ASR), speech translation (ST), language identification (LID), and voice activity detection (VAD). Models trained on this data (OWSM v4 series) are evaluated on multilingual ASR benchmarks (FLEURS, MLS, Common Voice), English ASR (Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard), long-form ASR, LID (FLEURS), and speech translation (CoVoST-2). The dataset supports both short-form (up to 30 seconds) and long-form speech processing.
